stack: SQLite through Python's sqlite3 (VS Code + its terminal)

tutorial.goal: learn SQL joins with SQLite: create tables, insert rows, INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN with GROUP BY

learner.notes: Every run really executes the learner's shop.py with this Python (sqlite3 is stdlib), so the rows printed are real.

outline.about: create the customers and orders tables
insert three customers and three orders

actions.note: four values for three columns: sqlite3.ProgrammingError (real)

actions.text: cur.executemany("INSERT INTO customers (id, name, city) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [(1, "Ada", "London", "UK"), (2, "Grace", "New York", "US"), (3, "Linus", "Helsinki", "FI")])

cur.executemany("INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, total) VALUES (?, ?)", [(1, 25.0), (1, 40.5), (2, 12.0)])
con.commit()
print("customers:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers").fetchone()[0])

outline.about: INNER JOIN orders to their customers

expect_checks.pattern: JOIN orders o ON o\.customer_id = c\.id

actions.note: joins on the wrong key (o.id = c.id): Grace gets Ada's order (real rows)

actions.text:
for row in cur.execute("SELECT c.name, o.total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.id = c.id ORDER BY o.id"):
    print(row)

outline.about: LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY: every customer with order count and total

actions.note: uses an INNER JOIN, so Linus (no orders) disappears (real rows)

actions.find: FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY
actions.replace: FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY
